all.name: Nifty 50
findings: Nifty 50 rose on 53% of days and over 71% of 1-year windows (1990–2026, 8,823 days).
After an up day the next day rose 57% of the time; after a down day 48% (yesterday's direction tends to continue).
Day-to-day momentum (lag-1 autocorrelation) by decade: 1990s +0.12, 2000s +0.08, 2010s +0.07, 2020s -0.06. Positive means trends persisted day to day; near zero means the market became efficient.
Strongest next-day effect: after '+1..2%' (1128 cases) the next day rose 63% vs 53% normally (z = +6.7).
When Nifty 50 was > 40% below its peak, it was higher a year later 93% of the time (avg +59%), vs 71% for any day.
Volatility clusters: after a top-10% move, the next day was also a top-10% move 28% of the time (vs 10% normally). Big moves come in bunches, so size option trades smaller after a shock.
After a new 52-week high, the next 20 days were up 60% of the time (avg +2.1% vs +1.3% for any day): highs tend to lead to more highs.

Tested 50 technical, pattern and calendar rules on 88,886 trading days across 10 markets.

9 passed every check (positive on Nifty in all three periods, better than 95% of random timings, positive in other markets): EMA 9/21 cross, Price vs SMA 20, Price vs SMA 50, Price vs SMA 100, MACD above/below zero, MA ribbon (5 averages), RSI 14 above/below 50, 3-month momentum, Turn of month (last + first 3 days).

32 failed. Most mean-reversion rules (RSI-2, streak fading, IBS, Bollinger reversal) and candlestick patterns lost money on Indian indices: the Indian market has rewarded following moves more than fading them.
No single rule beat simply holding Nifty on risk-adjusted terms in the last decade (buy & hold holdout Sharpe 0.70). Trend edges were much stronger in 1990–2005 than they are now.

The combined algorithm (21 rules, chosen only from pre-2006 data), long-only, on Nifty since 2016: 4.7% a year, Sharpe 0.74, worst fall -9%, vs buy & hold 10.5%, Sharpe 0.70, worst fall -38%. It mainly cuts the big drawdowns. It does not raise returns.
Turn-of-month (last day + first 3 days of each month) was positive in every period and every market tested, the most consistent calendar effect.
